I have been asked by my teacher to explain (prove my comprehension) of this
memory state diagram:

![Python Understanding Variables](./python-understanding-variables)

I'll explain it through commented Python code.

```python
# Do note that there are differences between how this would execute in a
# Python interpreter, and what is represented by the diagram.
#
# The comments describe the diagram rather than the code.

# This is likely programmed in C++, rather than Python which has a more
#   niche memory setup.
#
# Consistencies:
# - Strings are not literals, instead they are stored as pointers and
#   kept elsewhere in memory.
# - Integers and booleans are literals; they are stored inside their
#   parent objects.
# - Lists are pointed to, rather than stored inside their parent classes.
#   If this is C++, `Vector`s are likely used instead of literal lists.
#
# User 0 and user 3 both have the song "Theme song" in their playlists;
#   the arrays share the same object to represent that.


class Song:
    def __init__(self, title: str, duration: int, favourite: bool) -> None:
        self.title = title
        self.duration = duration
        self.favourite = favourite


class Account:
    def __init__(
        self, login: str, password: str, playlist: list[Song]
    ) -> None:
        self.login = login
        self.password = password
        self.playlist = playlist


class Users:
    def __init__(self, accounts: list[Account]) -> None:
        self.accounts = account


if __name__ == "__main__":
    theme_song = Song("Theme Song", 137, True)

    users = Users(
        [
            Account("Ahmed231", "scruffy", [None, theme_song, None, None]),
            None,
            None,
            Account(None, None, [None, None, None, theme_song]),
        ]
    )
```
